context: Forking a default lens is the documented tuning path. This scenario checks the fork keeps what it should, drops what was asked, adds a dimension that meets the lens bar, and that selection semantics are stated correctly.

checklist.name: Starts from the default lens
checklist.description: The fork keeps the default lens's structure (scope, method, threshold, reporting) and its remaining dimensions (load, data volume, concurrency, dependency failure, duplicate execution) recognisably intact

checklist.name: Rollout dimension removed
checklist.description: The fork contains no instruction about rollouts, mixed old-and-new versions, or deployment ordering

checklist.name: Idempotency dimension has a bar
checklist.description: The added dimension states a consequence-based bar: a retry or duplicate delivery can cause a charge, refund, or ledger write to happen more than once, named as money moving twice or a ledger disagreeing with the processor

checklist.name: Idempotency dimension has an exclusion
checklist.description: The fork names cases that resemble the concern and are fine, such as writes already guarded by an idempotency key or a unique constraint, or reads

checklist.name: Local iteration command
checklist.description: usage.md gives tessl code review --skill ./review-lenses/review-scale-and-resilience-payments (a local path) for iterating

checklist.name: Complete pinned lens set
checklist.description: usage.md's lenses input names all four lenses that should run: the three remaining defaults as pinned tessl/code-review@<version>#... refs plus the fork, and says the input replaces the defaults rather than adding to them

checklist.name: Fork is not a registry ref
checklist.description: usage.md does not invent a registry ref for the fork; it references the fork by repository path, or says publishing it as a plugin is the step that would give it one
